blindSummary:
This country is safe in practice for trans visitors, thin in law. A regional LGBTI-rights index lists it among states with no functioning legal gender recognition process (a resident-facing gap only). There is no criminalisation, no bathroom law, no border friction (an open border with the single neighbouring state that entirely surrounds it), and no documented pattern of anti-trans violence in this tiny, tourism-dependent republic.

The practical picture combines very high de facto safety with minimal explicit legal infrastructure for trans people. Assessment caveat: very small jurisdiction with limited data. Single incidents and absent documentation carry correspondingly little evidential weight; do not over-interpret sparse data in either direction.
blindOutOfScope: Absent legal gender recognition is resident-facing.
blindSourceSummaries: Regional LGBTI-rights index page on legal gender recognition (2026): this country is listed among states with no functioning legal or administrative process for legal gender recognition; self-determination-based recognition exists in 12 countries in the region.

Regional LGBTI-rights organisation annual review 2026 - legal gender recognition chapter: country-by-country findings for 2025, including one state's rejection of a self-ID recommendation at a UN review, a trans activist's legal action in another state, a delayed hormone-treatment decree in a third, and other regional developments.

Compilation by the same organisation of SOGIESC recommendations from the 34th session of a UN human-rights review working group (Nov 2019) - includes this country's review among 12 countries examined; documents the SOGIESC recommendations each state received and accepted.
Pan-regional news outlet (June 2019): this country banned discrimination based on sexual orientation (page largely navigation content at fetch time).

Foreign broadsheet (April 2022): this country appointed the world's first openly gay head of state - an openly gay legislator was named one of the country's two rotating joint heads of state, amid coverage of the country's strides on gay rights.

Regional news outlet (Nov 2018): this country approved a civil-unions law, narrower than the recent relationship-recognition law of the large neighbouring state that surrounds it - the legislative milestone for relationship recognition.
blindLocalsOnly: No functioning legal gender recognition process — resident-facing gap.
